newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends down; stock plunge causes outflows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends down; stock plunge causes outflows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed at an 11-month low against its U.S. counterpart on Thursday as a politically-induced stock market tumble triggered outflows of funds to overseas markets, dealers said.
The local unit reversed its earlier gains and closed at T$27.787 to one U.S. dollar against Wednesday's T$27.771 close.
It was the Taiwan dollar's lowest close since a T$27.790 finish on June 8, 1996.

The island's stock market plunged by 2.27 percent on Thursday as hectic selling was triggered by recent political instability amid public discontent over the government's failure to check a spate of violent murders.
Similar stock sell-offs also had caused the Taiwan dollar to fall on Monday and Tuesday before it rebounded slightly on Wednesday.
"When a stock market plunges like that, some funds are bound the leave the island," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said they expected a stable rate for Friday. A T$27.76-80 range was seen. -- Kevin Chen (5080815)
